title: head-size sets the size of a connector's heads
body:
Today a connector's heads have a fixed size. In `crates/acre/src/scene/connector.rs`, `head_len` makes a triangle or open head `8 + 3 × stroke-width` pixels long, and `dot_radius` gives a dot a radius of `2.5 + 1.5 × stroke-width`. The shaft's length caps both. `arrow`, `line` and `polyline` all draw their heads through `draw_shaft`, so none of them can change the size.

A figure with many thin arrows close together needs smaller heads. The sufr pipeline figure in `sufr-figures` draws about 100 arrows at stroke width 1.2 into a row of 8 px slots. Their 11.6 px heads overlap into a solid band.

## Proposal

`arrow`, `line` and `polyline` take `head-size N`, in pixels. It sets the length of a triangle or open head, and the diameter of a dot, at both `head` and `tail`. Without it the sizes stay as they are. The shaft's length still caps them.

## Rejected

- A scale factor such as `head-scale 0.5`. It would keep dots and triangles in proportion without a unit, but every other size in acre is in pixels.
- Relying on `stroke-width`. A thinner stroke shrinks the head only a little. At width 0.5 a triangle is still 9.5 px long.
close_reason: Landed in 283ff9d on dev, as proposed.
